transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ari Kaplan (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO - Novus Edge), Lena Cho (Infra Lead), Marco Rivera (Security)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment options for Novus Edge: VPC peering vs PrivateLink/Private Endpoints, region availability, IP addressing and CIDR constraints, KMS/HSM requirements, and performance expectations. Agreed to share security pack and schedule technical benchmarking deep-dive.

Topics:
- VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink / Private endpoints
- Region constraints and data residency (EU vs US regions)
- Network egress, NAT, and firewall rules
- KMS / HSM and key control for customer data
- Dedicated vs Private capacity and autoscaling expectations

Transcript:
[00:00] Ari: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ari Kaplan from Redwood Inference, AE on the West coast, with me is Sofia our solutions engineer. Uh, quick intro?
[00:07] Samir: Hi Ari, thanks. Samir Patel here, CTO at Novus Edge. Lena and Marco on the call too.
[00:12] Lena: Hey all.
[00:14] Marco: Marco Rivera, security.
[00:16] Sofia: Hi everyone, Sofia Ramos. We'll try to keep this practical - network, security, and region constraints up front.

[00:30] Ari: Objective for today is to understand your networking constraints for Private/VPC deploy - whether you want VPC peering or private endpoints, region restrictions, and anticipated throughput. Do I have that right, Samir?
[00:40] Samir: Yeah that's right. We're evaluating three options: Redwood hosted API is easiest, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private VPC for strict data control. At this stage Private is preferred if we can meet our compliance and internal networking rules.

[01:05] Lena: Quick background - we run most infra in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Sensitive PII workloads must stay in eu-central-1. We also have strict firewall egress rules - only certain IP ranges allowed outbound and we terminate TLS at our gateway.
[01:20] Marco: From security side we'll need customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), audit logs shipped to our SIEM, SSO with SAML, RBAC, encryption/KMS, and IP allowlists for any private endpoints. Also SOC 2 type II is required.

[01:45] Sofia: Makes sense. For Private deployment we offer a customer VPC option where Redwood runs inference nodes in a private VPC peered to your account, or we can expose private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) so the traffic never traverses the public internet. Both have tradeoffs - peering gives lower latency but requires route table changes; PrivateLink is simpler for cross-account but adds per-ENI costs.

[02:10] Ari: Do you have a preference between peering and PrivateLink, or are you evaluating?
[02:14] Samir: We're evaluating. Our networking team prefers peering because of predictable IP ranges, but our security team likes PrivateLink because we avoid editing route tables. Marco?
[02:22] Marco: PrivateLink is attractive but we need support for interface endpoints in eu-central-1; some vendors only deploy in certain regions which is an issue. Also we want control over KMS keys so encryption-at-rest keys are our KMS.

[02:45] Sofia: On KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS keys in most deployments; for HSM-backed keys we can integrate via your cloud HSM or a supported KMS provider, though that has some onboarding work and a bit more latency on key access. We can document the flow.

[03:10] Lena: Region availability - you mentioned earlier Redwood has runtime in eu-central-1?
[03:15] Ari: Yes we have hosts in eu-central-1 and us-west-2; however specific model variants and Dedicated pools availability can vary. For eu-central-1 we support the standard models and our Private deployment can be colocated there - it's a common ask for EU data residency.
[03:32] Samir: Good. Any limits on private endpoints per account? We have a VPC architecture with multiple availability zones and a central NAT - NAT egress must remain in our control.
[03:42] Sofia: We can support endpoints in each AZ, and we respect your NAT/egress controls. For egress-sensitive customers we can place the outbound traffic through your NAT gateway so you observe egress. That requires route table and probably an interface endpoint or peering configuration.

[04:10] Marco: How do you handle IP allowlisting? Do you require us to open ranges on our firewall?
[04:15] Ari: For peering we share a small set of CIDR ranges used by the Redwood nodes in your VPC; you add them to route tables and firewall rules. For PrivateLink we provide our endpoint service name and you create interface endpoints; less CIDR exchange but you still may need to open specific ports in the security groups.
[04:35] Lena: Are there implications for cross-region failover? We need canary region in case eu-central-1 is degraded. Can Redwood route to us-west-2 in emergencies while ensuring data stays in EU?
[04:47] Sofia: By default cross-region fallback would cross regions, yes. For strict residency we can configure policy to fail instead of failover, or route to a mirrored eu region if available. We also offer logging and tracing so you can detect any automatic fallback.

[05:10] Samir: Performance: our target p99 latency for interactive flows is sub-200ms. We're concerned about extra hops if using PrivateLink or peering with NAT. Can you share benchmarks?
[05:20] Sofia: We'll share our latency profiles; in practice peering with local hosts yields lower latency - PrivateLink adds a small extra hop and ENI overhead, typically adding 10-30ms depending on region. Dedicated pools in-region with pinned model versions are the best path for predictable p99.

[05:45] Ari: To help us size, what's your expected QPS and token distribution?
[05:49] Samir: Initially low - about 5 QPS with spikes to 25, token lengths variable, average 60 tokens per request. We'll likely run a pilot with 4-6 models across teams.

[06:05] Sofia: That sizing can be handled by a small dedicated pool, auto-scale setpoints we can tune. For cost we'll model both Dedicated reserved and Private - Private tends to have an infra/setup fee plus monthly runtime, but keeps data in your VPC.

[06:25] Lena: Onboarding - what network changes do you need from us to start a pilot?
[06:29] Ari: Minimal if you choose PrivateLink - create interface endpoints for the service we provide and open the security group ports we specify. For peering, create peering connection and update routes. We'll send a step-by-step doc.

[06:45] Marco: Audit logs and SIEM - can we ship full access logs to our CloudWatch/CloudTrail or S3 for our SIEM?
[06:53] Sofia: Yes we can forward audit logs and request traces. Private deployments can write logs into your S3 or push to your logging endpoint. We also support syslog/SIEM integration with our observability add-on.

[07:10] Samir: Ok, about the KMS flow - if we use customer-managed key, do you ever hold the plaintext?
[07:16] Ari: No, Redwood's runtime keeps encrypted model cache and data-at-rest encrypted with your key; for keys managed by you we use envelope encryption and we don't persist plaintext keys. There's a brief handshake on key policy setup but we can share the exact flow.

[07:36] Marco: If you need to access telemetry or traces for debugging, what's the process?
[07:40] Sofia: We can set up masked traces or allow access to sanitized logs; any access is via an audit trail and we can do role-based access. We also recommend running a short scoped bench with limited sample data.

[08:05] Ari: Any regulatory or compliance constraints besides SOC2 and data residency?
[08:09] Marco: We'll need to confirm GDPR processing terms and possibly DPA, and for some customers we have additional contractual clauses around subprocessor access.

[08:20] Sofia: We have DPA and subprocessors documented; we'll include that in the security pack.

[08:35] Lena: Networking detail: our VPCs use /16 ranges in both regions, and we have a central transit gateway. Do you support peering into transit gateways or do you need per-VPC peering?
[08:46] Ari: We can peer to a Transit Gateway in many cases, but some cloud accounts require a per-VPC approach. We'll need the account ID and TGW IDs to validate. That is one of the items Marco can share.

[09:05] Samir: Is there any special setup for egress billing or NAT? We want egress to still pass through our NAT for auditing.
[09:12] Sofia: Yes, if you want egress to be observable we can route through your NAT - that will add minimal latency but preserves your egress audit and any proxies. We can document the route table changes.

[09:35] Marco: What about PKI / mTLS for service-to-service? We prefer mutual TLS where possible.
[09:40] Ari: We support TLS and can enable mTLS for service endpoints. That typically requires certificate exchange and we can integrate with your internal PKI or manage certs in the endpoint configuration.

[10:00] Lena: Any limitations on number of interface endpoints or ENIs? We plan to create interface endpoints in every AZ, that's like 6 endpoints.
[10:07] Sofia: Should be fine; AWS does have soft limits but most customers are well within default quotas. We'll note that if you have strict quotas, request increases early.

[10:25] Samir: Are there automation templates? Terraform, CloudFormation?
[10:28] Ari: Yep - we provide Terraform modules and CFN snippets for both peering and PrivateLink, plus a step-by-step runbook. We'll share those in the pack.

[10:40] Marco: About model versions - if we pin a version for reliability, can you rollback quickly? We need rollback policies for safety.
[10:47] Sofia: We support version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. Rollbacks are orchestrated via our control plane and we can set automatic fallback to a previous pinned model to avoid regressions.

[11:05] Ari: Anything we haven't covered?
[11:08] Lena: One more - latency SLA. Do you offer SLOs for p99 under Dedicated or Private?
[11:13] Sofia: We offer latency and availability SLAs for Dedicated customers; for Private we can include SLA on a case-by-case basis depending on reserved capacity and region.

[11:30] Samir: On pricing - high level expectation is helpful: what's the delta between Dedicated reserved and Private?
[11:37] Ari: Private typically has a setup/onboarding fee and a slightly higher per-hour node cost because of isolation - but you avoid data egress fees if everything stays in your VPC. Reserved Dedicated gives predictable throughput for lower unit cost. We'll provide a comparison doc with numbers based on your pilot sizing.

[12:00] Marco: Any specific network ports needed?
[12:03] Sofia: We'll send a minimal list - typically HTTPS (443) for API and a few internal ports for health checks. Nothing exotic.

[12:20] Samir: Ok, timeline - we'd like to pilot in eu-central-1 by end of June if possible. Is that realistic?
[12:27] Ari: Yes, with quick onboarding and the details you provide (VPC IDs, CIDRs, account IDs) we can target a late June pilot. We'll need the security pack done and the network ready.

[12:45] Sofia: For the technical deep-dive, we'll want your infra team present - propose 60-90 minute bench session to validate p99, throughput, and cold-start behavior.

[13:00] Lena: We'll get the infra folks lined up.

[13:04] Ari: Recap / next steps - we'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO, DPA), Terraform snippets, and a preliminary pricing sketch. Marco to send VPC details and TGW IDs. Sofia will schedule the benchmark deep-dive.

[13:24] Marco: Sounds good. Also sending firewall contact.

[13:30] Samir: Thanks Ari and Sofia.

[13:33] Ari: Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.

[13:40] --- End of recorded segment ---

Notes on transcription: Some product names may be transcribed slightly off (e.g., PrivateLink sometimes rendered as "private link"). Speaker labels are from calendar and manual additions may differ.
